tasks.title: Open the watch table
tasks.body:
1. In TIA’s left Project tree, under this PLC, expand Watch and force tables. Double-click Add new watch table. It is alongside Program blocks, not inside OB1.
  2. In the new table, click the first blank Address cell. Enter these six addresses, one per row. Leave Modify value blank.
  3. Click the glasses button above this grid whose tooltip says Monitor all. Read Monitor value. Press Ctrl+S to save the table; this step needs no download.
AddressMeaning
DB98.DBX112.7Closing command
Q44.0Closing output
DB94.DBX29.4Robot permission
I505.7Robot input
DB200.DBX38.2Servo selection
DB200.DBX49.3EUROMAP selection

Read only. Do not force or change any of these machine bits.

tasks.title: Match the closing bit to the machine
tasks.body:
1. Have the operator identify the start of a production cycle over the phone.
  2. Watch DB98.DBX112.7 and Q44.0. Record when they turn TRUE and whether there is another pulse later in the same cycle.

tasks.title: Match the robot return to cycle end
tasks.body:
1. Watch DB94.DBX29.4 and I505.7. Record the low state and the return to TRUE.
  2. Have the operator confirm whether that return is when the robot is done and clear. Save your photos/times in the notes. Do not mark a robot sequence verified from manual closing alone.

tasks.title: Record the three reporting conditions
tasks.body: Record the existing production-eligible, robot-data-valid and abort tags. Leave unresolved items blank. These machines need their own reviewed source mapping; do not import the MM6 V2 source unchanged.

tasks.title: Create the CSI folder for the new blocks
tasks.body:
1. Work in a saved copy of the current MM6 project. In Program blocks, check the names listed below. If an earlier CSI2 installation is already present, do not create over it or change its running instance type; use a separate learning copy for review.
  2. Right-click Program blocks → Add new group. Name the new group CSI if that group name is unused. It is an organizing folder, not executable logic. If CSI is already someone else’s group, use CSI reporting without renaming theirs.
  3. The main function block you will create is CSI_Reporting. The other small blocks listed below supply its clock, stored values and reusable counters. Follow the checklist in order.
  4. Create each block through Add new block as its step says. If TIA puts it at the root of Program blocks, drag only that new block into your CSI group. Leave all existing blocks where they are.

These steps use SCL for the new code and keep OB1 in its existing language. The logic is the V2 design, entered by hand; it remains uncompiled in TIA and untested on the PLC. No import is required.

tasks.title: Build the three small helper functions
tasks.body:
Create and compile these one at a time. Each has its own interface grid and code area.

CSI2_DayNumber
  1. In TIA’s left Project tree → this MM6 PLC → Program blocks, double-click Add new block. Choose Function (FC).
  2. Enter Name = CSI2_DayNumber. Leave block-number assignment on Automatic; record the number TIA assigns. Do not replace an occupied block.
  3. Select Language = SCL, enable Add new and open, then OK. This only creates the new block; it does not change OB1’s language.
  4. In the upper interface grid, expand Return. Change the existing return row’s Data type to DInt. Do not add a second Output named RET_VAL. TIA may display the return as the function name or Ret_Val.

Enter these in the upper declaration grid, not the code area below. Expand the named section and click its first <Add new> Name cell. Enter Name, Data type, and the shown Start/Default value. Leave a dash at the TIA default. Type names without #, quotation marks, or semicolons.

Input · 3 rows
NameData typeStart / defaultComment
YearInt—
MonthInt—
DayInt—
Temp · 5 rows

Temp rows have no retained/start value to enter. They are working values for this execution of the block.

Code goes in the large SCL editor below the interface grid. Pull the horizontal divider down if the grid is hidden. Enter the sections below in order, appending each one beneath the previous one in the same block. Do not replace earlier sections, create a new FB per section, or paste declarations into this area.

Enter the code

Convert a valid calendar date into a comparable day number; -1 means the date is invalid.

    #CSI2_DayNumber := -1;
    IF (#Year < 1990) OR (#Year > 2089) OR (#Month < 1) OR (#Month > 12) THEN RETURN; END_IF;
    #leap := ((#Year MOD 4) = 0) AND (((#Year MOD 100) <> 0) OR ((#Year MOD 400) = 0));
    #y := INT_TO_DINT(#Year) - 1;
    #ordinal := #y * 365 + #y / 4 - #y / 100 + #y / 400;
    FOR #m := 1 TO #Month DO
        CASE #m OF
            4,6,9,11: #md := 30;
            2: IF #leap THEN #md := 29; ELSE #md := 28; END_IF;
            ELSE #md := 31;
        END_CASE;
        IF #m < #Month THEN #ordinal := #ordinal + INT_TO_DINT(#md); END_IF;
    END_FOR;
    IF (#Day < 1) OR (#Day > #md) THEN RETURN; END_IF;
    #CSI2_DayNumber := #ordinal + INT_TO_DINT(#Day) - 726468;

Check: after all sections are entered, press Ctrl+S. Right-click this block in the tree → Compile → Software (only changes). Read the Compile pane; double-click the first error to go to its line. Resolve it before moving to the next block. Saving/compiling here does not download anything.

Code goes in the large SCL editor below the interface grid. Pull the horizontal divider down if the grid is hidden. Enter the sections below in order, appending each one beneath the previous one in the same block. Do not replace earlier sections, create a new FB per section, or paste declarations into this area.

Enter the code

Add the scan’s elapsed milliseconds. Carry whole seconds into Seconds and keep the remaining milliseconds in Millis.

    // Seconds + remainder prevents the 24.8-day DINT-millisecond limit.
    #Millis := #Millis + #DeltaMs;
    #carry := #Millis / 1000;
    #Millis := #Millis MOD 1000;
    IF #Seconds <= 2147483647 - #carry THEN
        #Seconds := #Seconds + #carry;
    ELSE
        #Seconds := 2147483647;
        #Millis := 999;
        "CSI2_Report".TimingFault := 1;
    END_IF;

Input · 7 rows

Temp rows have no retained/start value to enter. They are working values for this execution of the block.

Code goes in the large SCL editor below the interface grid. Pull the horizontal divider down if the grid is hidden. Enter the sections below in order, appending each one beneath the previous one in the same block. Do not replace earlier sections, create a new FB per section, or paste declarations into this area.

1. Validate the period and close its previous count

This code is reused for the hour, day, shift 1 and shift 2. Each call will have its own stored state.

    IF NOT #ClockOK THEN
        IF #HaveCurrent AND NOT #Closed THEN #CurrentPartial := TRUE; END_IF;
        #LastClockOK := FALSE;
        RETURN;
    END_IF;
    // Never relabel retained counts into an earlier period after clock rollback.
    IF #HaveCurrent AND (#KeyNow < #CurrentKey) THEN
        #CurrentPartial := TRUE;
        #LastClockOK := FALSE;
        RETURN;
    END_IF;
    #continuous := #ContinuityOK AND #LastClockOK
        AND ((#KeyNow = #LastSeenKey) OR (#KeyNow = #LastSeenKey + 1));
    IF #HaveCurrent AND NOT #Closed THEN
        IF NOT #continuous OR NOT #CollectionOK THEN #CurrentPartial := TRUE; END_IF;
        IF (#KeyNow <> #CurrentKey) OR NOT #WindowActive THEN
            // CLOSE OLD PERIOD BEFORE ADDING A BOUNDARY COMPLETION.
            #PreviousCount := #CurrentCount;
            #PreviousKey := #CurrentKey;
            #PreviousLabel := #CurrentLabel;
            #PreviousPartial := #CurrentPartial;
            #Closed := TRUE;
        END_IF;
    END_IF;
2. Start the new period and add a completed cycle

PreviousCount receives the old CurrentCount first. The new period starts at zero, then CountPulse adds one. A TRUE held robot signal is never used as CountPulse.

    IF #WindowActive THEN
        IF NOT #HaveCurrent OR (#KeyNow <> #CurrentKey) THEN
            #HaveCurrent := TRUE;
            #Closed := FALSE;
            #CurrentCount := 0;
            #CurrentKey := #KeyNow;
            #CurrentLabel := #LabelNow;
            #CurrentPartial := NOT #continuous OR NOT #CollectionOK;
        END_IF;
        IF NOT #Closed THEN
            IF NOT #CollectionOK OR NOT #continuous THEN #CurrentPartial := TRUE; END_IF;
            IF #CountPulse THEN
                #CurrentCount := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := #CurrentCount);
            END_IF;
        END_IF;
    END_IF;
    #LastSeenKey := #KeyNow;
    #LastClockOK := TRUE;

Check: after all sections are entered, press Ctrl+S. Right-click this block in the tree → Compile → Software (only changes). Read the Compile pane; double-click the first error to go to its line. Resolve it before moving to the next block. Saving/compiling here does not download anything.

Code goes in the large SCL editor below the interface grid. Pull the horizontal divider down if the grid is hidden. Enter the sections below in order, appending each one beneath the previous one in the same block. Do not replace earlier sections, create a new FB per section, or paste declarations into this area.

1. Startup, elapsed ticks and rising edges

The # names refer to this FB’s interface rows. PrevClose and PrevPermit remember the previous scan; closeRise and permitRise last only this scan.

    "CSI2_Report".SchemaVersion := 2;
    IF "CSI2_Report".Heartbeat >= 2147483647 THEN
        "CSI2_Report".Heartbeat := 0;
    ELSE
        "CSI2_Report".Heartbeat := "CSI2_Report".Heartbeat + 1;
    END_IF;
    #fresh := NOT #Initialized OR #Restart;
    #delta := 0;
    #tickOK := (#TickMs >= 0);
    IF #fresh THEN
        #Initialized := TRUE;
        #State := 0;
        #SyncLowSeen := FALSE;
        #CycleLowSeen := FALSE;
        #CycleSec := 0; #CycleMs := 0;
        #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
        #PrevClose := #CloseCommand;
        #PrevPermit := #RobotPermit;
        #PrevTick := #TickMs;
        #HaveUtc := FALSE;
        #LastClockWasOK := FALSE;
        "CSI2_Report".RestartEvents := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".RestartEvents);
    ELSIF #tickOK THEN
        #deltaLong := DINT_TO_LINT(#TickMs) - DINT_TO_LINT(#PrevTick);
        IF #deltaLong < 0 THEN #deltaLong := #deltaLong + LINT#2147483648; END_IF;
        IF (#deltaLong < 0) OR (#deltaLong > 10000) THEN
            #tickOK := FALSE;
            "CSI2_Report".TimingFault := 1;
        ELSE
            #delta := LINT_TO_DINT(#deltaLong);
        END_IF;
    END_IF;
    #PrevTick := #TickMs;
    #closeRise := #CloseCommand AND NOT #PrevClose AND NOT #fresh;
    #permitRise := #RobotPermit AND NOT #PrevPermit AND NOT #fresh;
    #qualified := #Enable AND #SignalsValid AND #tickOK AND NOT #fresh;
    #complete := FALSE;
    #boundary := FALSE;
2. Discard an aborted or invalid observation

This resets only the new observer’s unfinished timing. It does not reset the machine or erase held reporting history.

    // Losing trustworthy signal data cancels an observation, not held history.
    IF NOT #qualified OR #AbortCycle OR ((#State = 30) AND NOT #ProductionMode) THEN
        IF #State = 30 THEN
            "CSI2_Report".PartialObservationsSkipped := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".PartialObservationsSkipped);
        END_IF;
        #State := 0;
        #SyncLowSeen := FALSE;
        #CycleLowSeen := FALSE;
        #CycleSec := 0; #CycleMs := 0;
        #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
    END_IF;
3. Synchronize, time the cycle and save the completed duration

State 10 finds a known robot-return boundary. State 20 times the wait. State 30 times the whole cycle and ignores another close pulse. := copies a value, like MOVE; PreviousCycleSeconds is copied before the live timer is cleared.

    IF #qualified AND NOT #AbortCycle THEN
        IF #State = 0 THEN
            #State := 10;
            #SyncLowSeen := FALSE;
        END_IF;
        CASE #State OF
            10: // Synchronize: do NOT accept the first random closing pulse.
                IF #ProductionMode THEN
                    IF NOT #RobotPermit THEN #SyncLowSeen := TRUE; END_IF;
                    IF #SyncLowSeen AND #permitRise THEN
                        #boundary := TRUE;
                        #State := 20;
                        #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
                        #SyncLowSeen := FALSE;
                        "CSI2_Report".PartialObservationsSkipped := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".PartialObservationsSkipped);
                    END_IF;
                ELSE
                    #SyncLowSeen := FALSE;
                END_IF;
            20: // Known waiting gap keeps accumulating even while idle/manual.
                "CSI2_AddElapsed"(DeltaMs := #delta, Seconds := #GapSec, Millis := #GapMs);
                IF NOT #RobotPermit OR (#closeRise AND NOT #ProductionMode) THEN
                    // A new robot/manual operation without a measured start: resynchronize.
                    #State := 10;
                    #SyncLowSeen := NOT #RobotPermit AND #ProductionMode;
                    #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
                END_IF;
            30: // Whole-cycle elapsed time, NOT just valve-on time.
                "CSI2_AddElapsed"(DeltaMs := #delta, Seconds := #CycleSec, Millis := #CycleMs);
                IF NOT #RobotPermit THEN #CycleLowSeen := TRUE; END_IF;
                #complete := #CycleLowSeen AND #permitRise;
                IF #complete THEN
                    #boundary := TRUE;
                    "CSI2_Report".PreviousCycleSeconds := DINT_TO_REAL(#CycleSec) + DINT_TO_REAL(#CycleMs) / 1000.0;
                    "CSI2_Report".PreviousCycleValid := 1;
                    "CSI2_Report".TotalCompleted := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".TotalCompleted);
                    #State := 20;
                    #CycleSec := 0; #CycleMs := 0;
                    #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
                    #CycleLowSeen := FALSE;
                ELSIF #closeRise THEN
                    "CSI2_Report".IgnoredCloseEdges := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".IgnoredCloseEdges);
                END_IF;
        END_CASE;
        // If closing was already high BEFORE the clear boundary, its start was
        // not captured here. Skip that ambiguous next cycle; never start on its later pulse.
        IF #boundary AND #CloseCommand AND NOT #closeRise THEN
            #State := 10;
            #SyncLowSeen := FALSE;
            #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
        END_IF;
        // Finish/synchronize FIRST; accept the next start SECOND.
        // A simultaneous completion/start stores a zero observed between-cycle time.
        IF (#State = 20) AND #ProductionMode AND #RobotPermit AND #closeRise THEN
            "CSI2_Report".PreviousBetweenSeconds := DINT_TO_REAL(#GapSec) + DINT_TO_REAL(#GapMs) / 1000.0;
            "CSI2_Report".PreviousBetweenValid := 1;
            #State := 30;
            #CycleSec := 0; #CycleMs := 0;
            #GapSec := 0; #GapMs := 0;
            #CycleLowSeen := FALSE;
        END_IF;
    END_IF;
4. Read date fields and choose calendar inputs

Production quality is kept separate from the clock. LocalStamp supplies the local date/time; UtcStamp identifies repeated daylight-saving clock hours.

    #collectionOK := #qualified AND NOT #AbortCycle AND ((#State = 20) OR (#State = 30));

    // Calendar labels use LOCAL time. UTC hour identity distinguishes fall-back hours.
    // Assumption: plant uses a whole-hour UTC offset (Alabama Central time).
    #localDay := -1; #utcDay := -1;
    #hourKey := -1; #hourLabel := 0; #dateLabel := 0; #timeLabel := 0;
    #minuteOfDay := 0; #shift := 0;
    #shift1Key := -1; #shift2Key := -1;
    #shift1Active := FALSE; #shift2Active := FALSE;
    #calendarOK := #RawClockOK;
    IF #calendarOK THEN
        #localDay := "CSI2_DayNumber"(Year := UINT_TO_INT(#LocalStamp.YEAR), Month := USINT_TO_INT(#LocalStamp.MONTH), Day := USINT_TO_INT(#LocalStamp.DAY));
        #utcDay := "CSI2_DayNumber"(Year := UINT_TO_INT(#UtcStamp.YEAR), Month := USINT_TO_INT(#UtcStamp.MONTH), Day := USINT_TO_INT(#UtcStamp.DAY));
        #calendarOK := (#localDay >= 0) AND (#utcDay >= 0)
            AND (#LocalStamp.HOUR < 24) AND (#LocalStamp.MINUTE < 60) AND (#LocalStamp.SECOND < 60)
            AND (#UtcStamp.HOUR < 24) AND (#UtcStamp.MINUTE < 60) AND (#UtcStamp.SECOND < 60);
    END_IF;
5. Detect clock changes and select the shift

390 means 06:30; 1020 means 17:00; 360 means 06:00. Midnight does not restart the overnight shift. Do not alter these numbers while entering the code.

    #continuity := #LastClockWasOK AND #tickOK AND NOT #fresh;
    IF #calendarOK THEN
        #utcSecond := DINT_TO_LINT(#utcDay) * LINT#86400
            + USINT_TO_LINT(#UtcStamp.HOUR) * LINT#3600
            + USINT_TO_LINT(#UtcStamp.MINUTE) * LINT#60 + USINT_TO_LINT(#UtcStamp.SECOND);
        IF #HaveUtc THEN
            #clockStep := #utcSecond - #LastUtcSecond;
            IF #clockStep < 0 THEN
                // Wait until UTC catches up; preserve keyed history instead of relabeling it.
                #calendarOK := FALSE;
                #continuity := FALSE;
                "CSI2_Report".ClockReview := 1;
            ELSIF #clockStep > DINT_TO_LINT(#delta / 1000 + 2) THEN
                #continuity := FALSE;
                "CSI2_Report".ClockReview := 1;
            END_IF;
        END_IF;
        #hourKey := #utcDay * 24 + USINT_TO_DINT(#UtcStamp.HOUR);
        #minuteOfDay := USINT_TO_INT(#LocalStamp.HOUR) * 60 + USINT_TO_INT(#LocalStamp.MINUTE);
        #shift1Key := #localDay;
        IF #minuteOfDay < 390 THEN #shift1Key := #localDay - 1; END_IF;
        #shift2Key := #localDay;
        IF #minuteOfDay < 1020 THEN #shift2Key := #localDay - 1; END_IF;
        // Guard retained period identities across a restart with an earlier clock.
        IF (#hourKey < #HourCounter.CurrentKey) OR (#localDay < #DayCounter.CurrentKey)
           OR (#shift1Key < #Shift1Counter.CurrentKey) OR (#shift2Key < #Shift2Counter.CurrentKey) THEN
            #calendarOK := FALSE;
            #continuity := FALSE;
            "CSI2_Report".ClockReview := 1;
        END_IF;
        IF #calendarOK THEN
            #LastUtcSecond := #utcSecond;
            #HaveUtc := TRUE;
            #dateLabel := UINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.YEAR) * 10000
                + USINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.MONTH) * 100 + USINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.DAY);
            #timeLabel := USINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.HOUR) * 10000
                + USINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.MINUTE) * 100 + USINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.SECOND);
            #hourLabel := #dateLabel * 100 + USINT_TO_DINT(#LocalStamp.HOUR);
            #shift1Active := (#minuteOfDay >= 390) AND (#minuteOfDay < 1020);
            #shift2Active := (#minuteOfDay >= 1020) OR (#minuteOfDay < 360);
            IF #shift1Active THEN #shift := 1; ELSIF #shift2Active THEN #shift := 2; END_IF;
        END_IF;
    END_IF;
    IF NOT #calendarOK THEN
        #continuity := FALSE;
        "CSI2_Report".ClockReview := 1;
    END_IF;
    #LastClockWasOK := #calendarOK;
6. Update hour, day and both shift counters

All four instances receive the same one-scan complete bit. Each instance stores its previous period before adding a boundary completion to the new period.

    // Four independent buckets. Each rolls old values FIRST, then counts this completion.
    #HourCounter(ClockOK := #calendarOK, ContinuityOK := #continuity, CollectionOK := #collectionOK,
        KeyNow := #hourKey, LabelNow := #hourLabel, WindowActive := TRUE, CountPulse := #complete);
    #DayCounter(ClockOK := #calendarOK, ContinuityOK := #continuity, CollectionOK := #collectionOK,
        KeyNow := #localDay, LabelNow := #dateLabel, WindowActive := TRUE, CountPulse := #complete);
    #Shift1Counter(ClockOK := #calendarOK, ContinuityOK := #continuity, CollectionOK := #collectionOK,
        KeyNow := #shift1Key, LabelNow := #shift1Key, WindowActive := #shift1Active, CountPulse := #complete);
    #Shift2Counter(ClockOK := #calendarOK, ContinuityOK := #continuity, CollectionOK := #collectionOK,
        KeyNow := #shift2Key, LabelNow := #shift2Key, WindowActive := #shift2Active, CountPulse := #complete);
    IF #complete THEN
        "CSI2_Report".LastCycleEndDate := 0;
        "CSI2_Report".LastCycleEndTime := 0;
        IF #calendarOK THEN
            "CSI2_Report".LastCycleEndDate := #dateLabel;
            "CSI2_Report".LastCycleEndTime := #timeLabel;
            IF #shift = 0 THEN
                "CSI2_Report".GapCompleted := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".GapCompleted);
            END_IF;
        ELSE
            "CSI2_Report".ClockUnassigned := "CSI2_Increment"(Value := "CSI2_Report".ClockUnassigned);
        END_IF;
    END_IF;
7. Copy results to the Kepware reporting DB

These are MOVE-style assignments to the new CSI2_Report fields. Period identities and Partial flags stay paired with the counts.

    // Publish simple flat fields. Kepware reads these; it does not count PLC pulses.
    "CSI2_Report".CyclesThisHour := #HourCounter.CurrentCount;
    "CSI2_Report".CyclesPreviousHour := #HourCounter.PreviousCount;
    "CSI2_Report".ThisHourKeyUTC := #HourCounter.CurrentKey;
    "CSI2_Report".PreviousHourKeyUTC := #HourCounter.PreviousKey;
    "CSI2_Report".CurrentHourLocalLabel := #HourCounter.CurrentLabel;
    "CSI2_Report".PreviousHourLocalLabel := #HourCounter.PreviousLabel;
    "CSI2_Report".ThisHourPartial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#HourCounter.CurrentPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".PreviousHourPartial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#HourCounter.PreviousPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".CyclesToday := #DayCounter.CurrentCount;
    "CSI2_Report".CyclesPreviousDay := #DayCounter.PreviousCount;
    "CSI2_Report".TodayKeyLocal := #DayCounter.CurrentKey;
    "CSI2_Report".PreviousDayKeyLocal := #DayCounter.PreviousKey;
    "CSI2_Report".TodayPartial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#DayCounter.CurrentPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".PreviousDayPartial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#DayCounter.PreviousPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".Shift1Current := #Shift1Counter.CurrentCount;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift1Previous := #Shift1Counter.PreviousCount;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift1Day := #Shift1Counter.CurrentKey;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift1PreviousDay := #Shift1Counter.PreviousKey;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift1Partial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#Shift1Counter.CurrentPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".Shift1PreviousPartial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#Shift1Counter.PreviousPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".Shift2Current := #Shift2Counter.CurrentCount;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift2Previous := #Shift2Counter.PreviousCount;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift2Day := #Shift2Counter.CurrentKey;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift2PreviousDay := #Shift2Counter.PreviousKey;
    "CSI2_Report".Shift2Partial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#Shift2Counter.CurrentPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".Shift2PreviousPartial := BOOL_TO_DINT(#Shift2Counter.PreviousPartial);
    "CSI2_Report".CurrentShift := INT_TO_DINT(#shift);
    "CSI2_Report".LocalDateYYYYMMDD := #dateLabel;
    "CSI2_Report".LocalTimeHHMMSS := #timeLabel;
    "CSI2_Report".ClockValid := BOOL_TO_DINT(#calendarOK);
    "CSI2_Report".ObserverEnabled := BOOL_TO_DINT(#Enable);
    "CSI2_Report".SignalsValid := BOOL_TO_DINT(#SignalsValid);
    "CSI2_Report".ProductionMode := BOOL_TO_DINT(#ProductionMode);
    "CSI2_Report".AbortActive := BOOL_TO_DINT(#AbortCycle);
    "CSI2_Report".CloseCommand := BOOL_TO_DINT(#CloseCommand);
    "CSI2_Report".RobotPermit := BOOL_TO_DINT(#RobotPermit);
    "CSI2_Report".MonitorState := INT_TO_DINT(#State);
    "CSI2_Report".CycleActive := BOOL_TO_DINT(#State = 30);
    "CSI2_Report".BetweenActive := BOOL_TO_DINT(#State = 20);
    "CSI2_Report".Synchronized := BOOL_TO_DINT((#State = 20) OR (#State = 30));
    "CSI2_Report".CycleSeconds := DINT_TO_REAL(#CycleSec) + DINT_TO_REAL(#CycleMs) / 1000.0;
    "CSI2_Report".BetweenCycleSeconds := DINT_TO_REAL(#GapSec) + DINT_TO_REAL(#GapMs) / 1000.0;
8. Remember the inputs for the next scan

These two assignments must remain last, after using the old values for edge detection.

    #PrevClose := #CloseCommand;
    #PrevPermit := #RobotPermit;

Check: after all sections are entered, press Ctrl+S. Right-click this block in the tree → Compile → Software (only changes). Read the Compile pane; double-click the first error to go to its line. Resolve it before moving to the next block. Saving/compiling here does not download anything.

tasks.title: Create CSI_Reporting’s instance DB
tasks.body:
1. Compile CSI_Reporting first. In Program blocks → Add new block, choose Data block (DB).
  2. Enter Name = CSI2_MM6_Instance. In Type, select the function block CSI_Reporting instead of Global DB. Use automatic numbering and click OK.
  3. Open CSI2_MM6_Instance. TIA fills its members from CSI_Reporting’s interface; do not type those members a second time. If the fields are wrong, fix the FB interface and recompile.
  4. Keep this new instance optimized. Do not attach it to CSI2_CycleMonitor from the older import route. This manual route uses CSI_Reporting.

This DB is the main FB’s memory. Kepware will read the separate CSI2_Report DB, not this instance’s internal offsets.

tasks.title: Build the clock and MM6 input call
tasks.body:
1. In TIA’s left Project tree → this MM6 PLC → Program blocks, double-click Add new block. Choose Function (FC).
  2. Enter Name = CSI2_MM6_Run. Leave block-number assignment on Automatic; record the number TIA assigns. Do not replace an occupied block.
  3. Select Language = SCL, enable Add new and open, then OK. This only creates the new block; it does not change OB1’s language.
  4. Leave the function’s Return type as Void; it does not return a value through its name.

Enter these in the upper declaration grid, not the code area below. Expand the named section and click its first <Add new> Name cell. Enter Name, Data type, and the shown Start/Default value. Leave a dash at the TIA default. Type names without #, quotation marks, or semicolons.

Input · 3 rows
NameData typeStart / defaultComment
ProductionEligibleBool—
RobotDataValidBool—
AbortCycleBool—
Temp · 8 rows
NameData typeStart / defaultComment
localNowDTL—
utcNowDTL—
localRCInt—
utcRCInt—
tickDInt—
clockOKBool—
configOKBool—
enabledBool—

Temp rows have no retained/start value to enter. They are working values for this execution of the block.

Code goes in the large SCL editor below the interface grid. Pull the horizontal divider down if the grid is hidden. Enter the sections below in order, appending each one beneath the previous one in the same block. Do not replace earlier sections, create a new FB per section, or paste declarations into this area.

Enter the code

Read the clocks and the known MM6 bits, then run the new reporting FB through its instance DB. It reads the original machine addresses; it does not write them.

    // Call once at the approved end of OB1. Keep this call unconditional.
    // CONNECT THE THREE INPUT PINS TO VERIFIED MACHINE LOGIC. No addresses guessed.
    #tick := TIME_TO_DINT(TIME_TCK());
    #localRC := RD_LOC_T(OUT => #localNow);
    #utcRC := RD_SYS_T(OUT => #utcNow);
    #clockOK := ((#localRC = 0) OR (#localRC = 1)) AND (#utcRC = 0);
    #configOK := %DB200.DBX38.2 AND %DB200.DBX49.3;
    #enabled := "CSI2_Setup".Enable AND "CSI2_Setup".WiringReviewed AND #configOK;
    "CSI2_Report".ConfigurationOK := BOOL_TO_DINT(#configOK);
    "CSI2_MM6_Instance"(Enable := #enabled, Restart := "CSI2_Setup".StartupPending,
        CloseCommand := %DB98.DBX112.7, RobotPermit := %DB94.DBX29.6,
        ProductionMode := #ProductionEligible, SignalsValid := #RobotDataValid, AbortCycle := #AbortCycle,
        TickMs := #tick, RawClockOK := #clockOK, LocalStamp := #localNow, UtcStamp := #utcNow);
    "CSI2_Setup".StartupPending := FALSE;

Check: after all sections are entered, press Ctrl+S. Right-click this block in the tree → Compile → Software (only changes). Read the Compile pane; double-click the first error to go to its line. Resolve it before moving to the next block. Saving/compiling here does not download anything.

tasks.title: Build the startup-reset helper
tasks.body:
1. In TIA’s left Project tree → this MM6 PLC → Program blocks, double-click Add new block. Choose Function (FC).
  2. Enter Name = CSI2_MM6_Startup. Leave block-number assignment on Automatic; record the number TIA assigns. Do not replace an occupied block.
  3. Select Language = SCL, enable Add new and open, then OK. This only creates the new block; it does not change OB1’s language.
  4. Leave the function’s Return type as Void; it does not return a value through its name.

Enter these in the upper declaration grid, not the code area below. Expand the named section and click its first <Add new> Name cell. Enter Name, Data type, and the shown Start/Default value. Leave a dash at the TIA default. Type names without #, quotation marks, or semicolons.

Code goes in the large SCL editor below the interface grid. Pull the horizontal divider down if the grid is hidden. Enter the sections below in order, appending each one beneath the previous one in the same block. Do not replace earlier sections, create a new FB per section, or paste declarations into this area.

Enter the code

Set the new startup flag. The cyclic call consumes and clears it after initializing its own observer.

    // Append a call in the EXISTING applicable startup OB, normally OB100.
    // Do not replace that OB. Retained active timing must never span a restart.
    "CSI2_Setup".StartupPending := TRUE;

Check: after all sections are entered, press Ctrl+S. Right-click this block in the tree → Compile → Software (only changes). Read the Compile pane; double-click the first error to go to its line. Resolve it before moving to the next block. Saving/compiling here does not download anything.

tasks.title: Check report offsets and record its DB number
tasks.body:
1. In Program blocks, double-click CSI2_Report. Its grid contains the new tag names, types and offsets.
  2. Find PreviousCycleSeconds, BetweenCycleSeconds, CyclesThisHour and CyclesToday. Do not add, delete or reorder rows.
  3. Record the DB number shown beside CSI2_Report in the tree. Enter just that number below; Kepware needs it.

Confirm SchemaVersion byte 0, PreviousCycleSeconds byte 40, CyclesToday byte 156 and final field LastCycleEndTime byte 236. If any offset differs, fix row order/types in this new standard DB before using the Kepware map.

tasks.title: Add one call at the bottom of OB1
tasks.body:
1. In Program blocks, double-click OB1. Scroll to its last existing network. The analyzed MM6 has RobotMain / FC900 in network 48; leave that network unchanged.
  2. Right-click the last network’s heading → Insert network. Check that the empty network is below the existing code and outside a conditional jump. Name it Production reporting.
  3. If it is a text/STL network: click its first empty code line, type CALL "CSI2_MM6_Run", and press Enter. TIA inserts the three parameter lines.
  4. If it is a ladder/FBD network: drag CSI2_MM6_Run from Program blocks into the empty network. Leave its call unconditional; do not put an AUTO contact before it.

Use the form matching the editor already open. Do not convert OB1 to another language.

The actual path is OB1 → CSI2_MM6_Run → CSI2_MM6_Instance (CSI_Reporting). Add the wrapper once only; do not also call CSI_Reporting directly from OB1 or run the old imported observer in parallel.

tasks.title: Fill in the call’s three input tags
tasks.body:
Click beside each input on the new call and enter its verified existing BOOL tag or address:

InputConnect it to
ProductionEligibleTRUE for production to count, including approved manually started production; FALSE for setup/jog.
RobotDataValidTRUE while the robot/input data being read are valid and current.
AbortCycleTRUE when the measured cycle is canceled. Normal waiting is not an abort.

The closing and robot-permission addresses are already inside the wrapper. No extra pins are needed for them.

These three machine tags are still unverified. Leave this step unchecked and reporting disabled until they are resolved. Do not guess or use permanent TRUE values.

Offline compile values while mappings are unresolved

Enter FALSE for ProductionEligible, FALSE for RobotDataValid, and TRUE for AbortCycle. These deliberately prevent reporting. Replace all three before enabling.

tasks.title: Add the startup call
tasks.body:
1. Under Program blocks, open the existing Startup OB, normally OB100. Leave all its current logic in place.
  2. Insert a new network after its existing logic. In STL, type CALL "CSI2_MM6_Startup" and press Enter. In LAD/FBD, drag that FC into the new network. It has no input pins.
  3. If no startup OB exists, use Add new block → Organization block → Startup in the standard program, select an available startup OB, and insert the call there. Confirm this is the startup path for this CPU; do not create or edit an F-block.

tasks.title: Keep counts and times through restart
tasks.body:
1. Open CSI2_Report. In its declaration grid, use the Retain column to retain the new report data. For this standard-access DB, retention applies to the DB as a whole.
  2. Open CSI_Reporting. Expand its Static variables and configure retention for the four period-counter instances, including counts, keys and quality. Where retention is set in the instance DB, use CSI2_MM6_Instance. Retaining the full new instance is acceptable only if the CPU has capacity and the startup call above is installed.
  3. Keep CSI2_Setup.Enable and WiringReviewed FALSE for now. Compile and check any retention errors before proceeding.

If Retain is unavailable or the compiler rejects the selection, stop at that screen. Do not change retention on existing machine blocks.

tasks.title: Compile, save and review the download
tasks.body:
1. Right-click the PLC’s Program blocks → Compile → Software (only changes). Read the Compile results below the editor; double-click an error to open its location. Resolve every error.
  2. Press Ctrl+S. With the site-approved change window, choose Download to device → Software (only changes).
  3. Read Load preview. Verify the correct PLC, the new CSI/CSI2 blocks, and only the intended OB-call changes. Cancel unexpected STOP, hardware/F changes, deletions or initialization of existing DBs.
  4. Proceed only after that review. Keep reporting disabled until the next checks. Avoid running the earlier CSI observer and V2 as competing reporting sources.

Manually typed code needs the same full compile and load review as imported code. Do not load partially entered blocks.

tasks.title: Watch the new tags and check the PLC clock
tasks.body:
1. Create a separate new watch table under the MM6 PLC. In Name, enter each symbolic member below, or drag that member from its DB grid into the table.
  2. Click Monitor all. Require SchemaVersion = 2, ConfigurationOK = 1, ClockValid = 1, and the correct local date/time. The two Setup bits should still be FALSE.
  3. Check SignalsValid, ProductionMode and AbortActive against the three tags you wired. Do not turn reporting on if those meanings are wrong.

tasks.title: Enable the new reporting block
tasks.body:
1. Only after the input mappings and checks above are complete, use the new reporting watch table. Enter TRUE in Modify value for "CSI2_Setup".WiringReviewed and "CSI2_Setup".Enable.
  2. Select only those two rows. Use the normal Modify now / Modify selected values command, checking the tooltip and target rows first. Do not use Force.
  3. Confirm both Monitor values become TRUE. Clear their Modify value cells afterward so they cannot be resent accidentally.

This is the only planned write from the watch table: two NEW CSI2_Setup bits. Do not modify any original motion, permission or configuration bit.

tasks.title: Check the reported cycle and waiting times
tasks.body:
1. Add the report tags below to the reporting watch table and click Monitor all.
  2. Expect MonitorState 10 while synchronizing, 20 while between cycles, and 30 while timing. The first unknown partial cycle is deliberately skipped.
  3. Observe at least five normal cycles with someone at the machine. Each valid completion must update PreviousCycleSeconds and add exactly one to TotalCompleted. A second closing pulse inside the cycle must not restart or count another cycle.
  4. Check BetweenCycleSeconds during a real wait and PreviousBetweenSeconds after the next start. Confirm the period counts at a boundary or in an isolated test, then archive the finished TIA project.

tasks.title: Use this machine’s verified report DB
tasks.body: After its reporting code is installed and tested, record that machine’s report DB and offsets. Do not copy MM6’s DB number or V2 map into this device. Existing server notes and earlier checklist records are preserved under Completed.

tasks.title: Use this machine’s verified report DB
tasks.body: After its reporting code is installed and tested, record that machine’s report DB and offsets. Do not copy MM6’s DB number or V2 map into this device. Existing server notes and earlier checklist records are preserved under Completed.

tasks.title: Select the existing MM6 device
tasks.body:
1. Open the Kepware server configuration and save a backup of its project.
  2. In the left connection tree, select the existing MM6 device. Confirm its endpoint is MM6, not another machine.
  3. Use the address map here only with the Siemens TCP/IP Ethernet driver. A symbolic S7 Plus or OPC UA connection uses its own addressing. Do not change PLC security or hardware to make a connection work.

tasks.title: Create and test SchemaVersion
tasks.body:
1. Under MM6, right-click → New Tag Group → name it Production. Use the existing group if it is already there.
  2. Select Production → right-click → New Tag. Enter Name = SchemaVersion; Address = the SchemaVersion address in the map below; Data type = Long; Client access = Read Only; Scan rate = 1000 ms. Click Apply/OK.
  3. Open Tools → Launch OPC Quick Client (or the installed test client). Browse the MM6 Production group. Require Good quality and value 2. Stop and check the DB number, driver and access if it is not Good.

tasks.title: Add the time and count tags
tasks.body:
Repeat New Tag for the rows in the address map below. Use Long for DINT counts/status and Float for REAL seconds. Keep every tag Read Only.

Add Heartbeat and compare one time value with TIA before entering the remaining rows. The CSV is an address reference; for bulk import, export one tag from this Kepware version and use its exact CSV format.

tasks.title: Check the display and save Kepware
tasks.body:
1. Compare current/previous hour, day and both shift counts with TIA. Check PreviousCycleSeconds and both between-cycle values.
  2. Use BetweenActive for live waiting, the Valid fields for held values, and Partial/key fields for period quality. Do not display stale/bad-quality data as live.
  3. Save the Kepware project and record the real channel/device/group path. Export this checklist’s progress if you are moving to another computer.

schema.name: SchemaVersion
schema.description: Layout version; must read 2.

schema.name: Heartbeat
schema.description: Changes once per cyclic call; use client staleness checks.

schema.name: MonitorState
schema.description: 0 disabled/invalid; 10 synchronizing; 20 between cycles; 30 cycle active.

schema.name: CurrentShift
schema.description: 0 gap or invalid clock; 1 day; 2 night.

schema.name: CyclesThisHour
schema.description: Completed measured cycles in the current clock hour.

schema.name: CyclesPreviousHour
schema.description: Last observed closed hour; inspect its key and partial flag.

schema.name: Shift1Current
schema.description: Running/latest shift 1 count; resets at its next 06:30 start.

schema.name: Shift1Previous
schema.description: Last observed closed shift 1.

schema.name: Shift2Current
schema.description: Running/latest shift 2 count; does NOT reset at midnight.

schema.name: Shift2Previous
schema.description: Last observed closed shift 2.

schema.name: PreviousCycleSeconds
schema.description: Held duration from accepted closing start through robot return.

schema.name: BetweenCycleSeconds
schema.description: Live known gap; only current when BetweenActive=1.

schema.name: PreviousBetweenSeconds
schema.description: Held gap captured at the next accepted start.

schema.name: CycleSeconds
schema.description: Live measured cycle, diagnostic only.

schema.name: ThisHourKeyUTC
schema.description: UTC day serial since 1990-01-01 * 24 + UTC hour; identifies repeated DST hours.

schema.name: PreviousHourKeyUTC
schema.description: Key for CyclesPreviousHour; -1 means no history.

schema.name: Shift1Day
schema.description: Start date serial since 1990-01-01 for Shift1Current.

schema.name: Shift1PreviousDay
schema.description: Start date serial for Shift1Previous.

schema.name: Shift2Day
schema.description: START date serial for Shift2Current, including after midnight.

schema.name: Shift2PreviousDay
schema.description: START date serial for Shift2Previous.

schema.name: PreviousCycleValid
schema.description: 1 when a complete measured cycle populated the held value.

schema.name: PreviousBetweenValid
schema.description: 1 when a known gap populated the held value.

schema.name: ThisHourPartial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain current hour.

schema.name: PreviousHourPartial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain held hour.

schema.name: Shift1Partial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain running/latest day shift.

schema.name: Shift1PreviousPartial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain held day shift.

schema.name: Shift2Partial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain running/latest night shift.

schema.name: Shift2PreviousPartial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain held night shift.

schema.name: SignalsValid
schema.description: Verified robot/input communication qualification, supplied by caller.

schema.name: ClockValid
schema.description: 1 = local and UTC calendar usable for this scan.

schema.name: CycleActive
schema.description: 1 only in state 30.

schema.name: BetweenActive
schema.description: 1 only in state 20; gap is known.

schema.name: TimingFault
schema.description: Latched tick discontinuity or duration saturation.

schema.name: TotalCompleted
schema.description: All complete measured cycles since initialization; not a lifetime production total.

schema.name: GapCompleted
schema.description: Completions during 06:00 through 06:29:59 local.

schema.name: ClockUnassigned
schema.description: Measured completions not assigned to periods because clock was invalid.

schema.name: ClockReview
schema.description: Latched invalid/discontinuous calendar.

schema.name: CounterSaturated
schema.description: A DINT reporting counter reached its maximum; it never wraps negative.

schema.name: ObserverEnabled
schema.description: Status: setup enabled, wiring reviewed and expected configuration present.

schema.name: CyclesToday
schema.description: Local CALENDAR day, midnight to midnight.

schema.name: CyclesPreviousDay
schema.description: Last observed closed calendar day.

schema.name: TodayKeyLocal
schema.description: Current local date serial since 1990-01-01.

schema.name: PreviousDayKeyLocal
schema.description: Date serial for CyclesPreviousDay.

schema.name: TodayPartial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain current day.

schema.name: PreviousDayPartial
schema.description: 1 = incomplete/uncertain held day.

schema.name: LocalDateYYYYMMDD
schema.description: Readable current PLC local date.

schema.name: LocalTimeHHMMSS
schema.description: Readable current PLC local time; e.g. 63000 means 06:30:00.

schema.name: CurrentHourLocalLabel
schema.description: YYYYMMDDHH label, e.g. 2026092817; key UTC distinguishes repeated DST hour.

schema.name: PreviousHourLocalLabel
schema.description: Local label for held hour.

schema.name: PartialObservationsSkipped
schema.description: Synchronization boundaries/aborted active observations not counted as complete cycles.

schema.name: IgnoredCloseEdges
schema.description: Additional closing edges ignored while the current measured cycle was active.

schema.name: RestartEvents
schema.description: First-call/startup-reset events observed.

schema.name: ConfigurationOK
schema.description: Expected MM6 Servo and EUROMAP selectors both true.

schema.name: ProductionMode
schema.description: Verified production-eligibility input supplied by caller; setup/jog is excluded.

schema.name: AbortActive
schema.description: Verified observation-abort input supplied by caller.

schema.name: CloseCommand
schema.description: Snapshot of MM6 DB98.DBX112.7.

schema.name: RobotPermit
schema.description: Snapshot of MM6 DB94.DBX29.6.

schema.name: Synchronized
schema.description: 1 after a qualified robot low-to-high boundary has been observed.

schema.name: LastCycleEndDate
schema.description: Local YYYYMMDD at last measured completion; 0 if clock unavailable.

schema.name: LastCycleEndTime
schema.description: Local HHMMSS at last measured completion; inspect LastCycleEndDate for validity.

instructions.title: Where to enter tags and code
instructions.body:
New global tags: Program blocks → your new CSI2_Report DB → declaration rows.

FB/FC variables: open that new block → upper interface grid → Input, Output, InOut, Static or Temp, as its table specifies.

SCL logic: large text editor below that grid. #State is a local variable; "CSI2_Report".CyclesToday is a global DB member. := assigns/copies a value; = compares values.

Use the numbered MM6 tasks. Type the code or copy one section at a time. The code boxes contain executable body text only, not FUNCTION_BLOCK / VAR / BEGIN source-file wrappers.
